scope: Original owner-supplied upgrade list: 130 puzzles. Current source images inspected for 126 puzzles. Four code-rendered scenes (3, 338, 350, 450) need live visual review and are not graded here. Initial artwork was inspected; this is not an interaction or mobile playtest. These are subjective review candidates, not approved replacements.

items.title: Decorative frame template
items.reason: The two identical ornate plaques dominate the composition. Beside the stronger scene illustrations, this can feel like a reusable gold-sign template rather than a distinctive puzzle image.
items.suggestion: Consider a simpler, deliberately designed pair of adjacent objects or signs. Preserve the clear SIDE / SIDE relationship; extra detail is not the goal.

items.title: Too much empty space for tiny lettering
items.reason: Almost the whole square is empty, while RELATION and SHIP sit in small plaques at opposite edges. At card size the actual clue becomes much smaller than the surrounding decoration.
items.suggestion: Keep the wide separation, but enlarge the labels and strengthen the connecting visual. This may only need a composition adjustment, not a new concept.

items.title: Glossy text-effect look
items.reason: Faceted emerald letters and a strong glow give ENVY the look of a stock 3D title effect. The clue is clear, but the material treatment is less natural than the better illustrated scenes.
items.suggestion: Try restrained green enamel, painted lettering or a more intentional physical setting. Keep ENVY and the green colour immediately recognisable.

items.title: Generic geometric composition
items.reason: Repeated circles, cones and semicircles feel closer to a decorative stock graphic than a specific scene. It is cleanly made; the concern is its generic character, not its simplicity.
items.suggestion: Keep it if this graphic style suits your taste. Otherwise consider a tangible, equally balanced object split in two, preserving the break / even idea.

items.title: Where are the three strikes?
items.reason: The stadium and departing player are well illustrated. However, the three light towers show different lighting levels rather than three unmistakable strikes. A player could read this as leaving a game or lights going out.
items.suggestion: Preserve the stadium artwork and strengthen the three-strikes cue only if playtesting confirms confusion.

items.title: Day and night, but not clearly seven days
items.reason: The shop and day-to-night composition look polished. They communicate around-the-clock opening, but seven days is not explicit; several related phrases could fit the scene.
items.suggestion: Preserve the artwork. Consider a subtle seven-day cue if the current clues and answer pattern do not resolve the ambiguity.

items.title: Gloves are present; the fit is less obvious
items.reason: The sculptor scene is attractive, but the eye is drawn to the unusual sculpture. Wearing gloves does not by itself demonstrate an exceptionally close fit.
items.suggestion: Keep the visual quality. If needed, make the hand-and-glove fit the focal point instead of replacing the whole style.

items.title: Navigation is clearer than gratitude
items.reason: The sailor, stars and glowing route make a strong illustration. They suggest following a star or finding a safe route more directly than thanking lucky stars.
items.suggestion: Keep the artwork unless playtesting finds repeated confusion. A small, readable gesture of relief or gratitude could clarify the intended phrase.

items.title: The table reads as a mosaic game
items.reason: The group scene is well composed, but the colourful pieces resemble a geometric tile game. Playing cards and the idea of playing them right are not immediately distinct.
items.suggestion: Preserve the scene and consider clearer card shapes or a more deliberate successful move if the clue proves unfair.
